name: proof_01_level_sets
statement: For rho <= 0 the contextual mean is zero on each axis (essential domains); only rho > 0 lets one domain compensate for the absence of the other.
caption: Level sets of the contextual mean M(S, R) with equal weights for four members of the CES family. Markers are the three Table 1 profiles with the same arithmetic mean of 0.45. Curved level sets that meet the axes at zero show that a shortfall in one domain cannot be offset by the other.

name: proof_02_ces_family
statement: M_rho is non-decreasing in rho, equals the geometric mean at rho = 0, the arithmetic mean at rho = 1, and tends to min(S, R) as rho -> -infinity.
caption: The CES contextual mean against rho for the three Table 1 profiles. Dotted lines mark min(S, R), the bottleneck limit. The balanced profile is flat; the more unbalanced the profile, the more the choice of rho matters.

name: proof_03_capacity_ceiling
statement: 0 <= H <= P, with H = P only at S = R = 1 and H = 0 when either context domain is zero; H/P does not depend on the unit of P.
caption: Share of biomedical capacity realised, H/P, against social enablement for four levels of structural freedom (P = 30 in arbitrary units). The ceiling at one is reached only with both domains at one.

name: proof_04_balance_penalty
statement: At a fixed arithmetic mean of the context, the geometric score falls as the domains move apart (sqrt(0.45^2 - d^2)); the additive score does not move.
caption: H against the gap between the two context domains when their arithmetic mean is held at 0.45. Markers are the Table 1 profiles. Every non-compensatory member penalises imbalance.

name: proof_05_marginal_effects
statement: dH/dS = alpha H / S: the gain from social enablement is largest where S is low and R is high (complementarity, d2H/dSdR > 0).
caption: Analytic marginal effect of social enablement (lines) and central finite differences (open markers) for three levels of structural freedom, P = 1 and alpha = 0.5. The same gain in S is worth more when structural freedom is high.

name: proof_06_gap_decomposition
statement: log(H_a/H_b) = log(P_a/P_b) + alpha log(S_a/S_b) + (1 - alpha) log(R_a/R_b), exactly, with no residual.
caption: Exact log decomposition of the gap between two profiles that differ only in structural freedom (0.85 against 0.20), from results/gap.csv. The whole gap is structural, as it should be.

name: proof_07_determinacy_and_missingness
statement: With a known Gaussian model, determinacy rises with loadings and indicator count, and each missing indicator can only widen the posterior.
caption: Left: model-implied correlation between a single-factor score and its factor, by loading and number of indicators. Right: posterior standard deviation of the social domain in the three-domain synthetic model as its indicators go missing; with all three missing it borrows strength from the correlated domains and stays below the prior SD of one.

name: proof_08_measurement_drift
statement: A constant intercept shift moves every score by a fixed amount: correlation with the truth is unchanged while bias appears and interval coverage falls.
caption: Left: bias of the posterior social score as the intercepts of the social indicators drift, from the known-model formula (line) and from the 4,000-record simulation at a shift of 0.5 (marker). Right: coverage of 95% posterior intervals by domain and scenario, from results/measurement.csv; the dotted line is the nominal level.

name: proof_09_ede_aversion
statement: The Atkinson EDE falls from the weighted mean (epsilon = 0) through the weighted geometric mean (epsilon = 1) towards the minimum as epsilon grows; any zero gives EDE = 0 for epsilon >= 1.
caption: EDE of the population (0.1, 0.4, 0.9) against inequality aversion, unweighted and with three times the weight on the worst-off person. Dotted lines are the mean and the minimum.

name: proof_10_allocation_reversal
statement: With a fixed budget for one of two actions, the exact allocator's choice reverses once inequality aversion passes the point where the two EDE curves cross.
caption: EDE of H after each single action for the two-person example of Table 1 in paper 3. Below the crossing the larger total gain wins; above it the gain to the worse-off person wins. The exact enumeration in hpotential.crf.allocate picks the higher curve at every tabulated aversion.
